title: Rabbi Shmuel, Son of Rabbi Yose, Son of Rabbi Bon

paragraphs: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rabbi Yosi bar Rabbi Bon.

Hyman places him among the amoraim of the last generation in the Land of Israel, and in his days the academies of the Land of Israel had already been destroyed. He is further mentioned in the Yerushalmi: Demai ch. 4, end of halakhah 1; Rosh Hashanah ch. 1, halakhah 1, followed by the additional locator ג; Yevamot ch. 8, halakhah 3; Kiddushin ch. 4, halakhah 6; Horayot ch. 3, halakhah 5; and he said [a teaching] in the name of Rabbi Nasa, Ketubot ch. 7, end of halakhah 6.
And in Gittin ch. 5, halakhah 3: he and Rabbi Matanya were inclined to say [something]; Rabbi Yosi bar Rabbi Bon said to him — and he is Rabbi Yosi bar Rabbi Bon the latter.

notes.text: The later Yose bar Bon is Hyman’s explicit identification. The shortened Nasa name is retained without a new identity claim.

The Rosh Hashanah locator reads פ״א ה״א-ג. The translation retains chapter 1, halakhah 1 and the additional ג without assuming a range of halakhot 1–3. The last-generation chronology and destruction of the academies are Hyman’s account.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5:3 names Shmuel, son of Yose bar Bon, with Matanya, and says Yose bar Bon spoke “to them.” Hyman’s supplied “to him” is retained. The later-Yose identification and academy chronology remain his account.
